h.strategy: Naive reasoning predicts substitution: if something similar exists elsewhere, an edit helps less. Experts find this obvious, so at most two hypotheses may use it. At least three hypotheses must predict the opposite, complementarity, where an edit helps MORE because a different kind of component elsewhere supplies what it lacks. At least two must predict a reversal, where a usually beneficial edit becomes harmful under a specific condition through trainability, merged-signal scale, or over-capacity. Never condition on the edited field's own value or on settings that make the edit inert. Each hypothesis must couple two different fields, and no condition setting may appear more than twice. In each 'why', give the mechanism in two or three sentences, state why an expert might bet the other way, and name the refuting comparison. The critic should replace any hypothesis that duplicates another's mechanism.

hyps.why: Two identity routes into node 3 are redundant, so the second skip adds little compared with when edge 3 is a conv.
Replacing a missing edge 5 restores the node 2 to output path, a larger gain than swapping one existing op for a conv.
A strong direct 3x3 conv from input to output already provides the spatial features the node 2 route would add.
Replacing a missing direct input-to-output edge with an identity path restores a key gradient route, whereas replacing any existing op yields a much smaller or negative change.
With edge 0 absent node 1 is dead, so adding a conv there activates the whole node-1 subgraph, a far bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Replacing the highly useful identity shortcut with a conv gains less (or loses) compared with replacing weaker ops on edge 3.
When a direct skip already gives node 3 a strong shortcut, a deep conv on edge 5 contributes less than when edge 3 is none or pool.
With edge 0 absent, edge 1 is the main way into node 2 and its downstream edge, so its conv matters much more.
With edge 0 absent node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 2 has almost no effect compared with when node 1 is fed.
With edge 0 absent node 1 is dead, so a conv on edge 4 is nearly inert, unlike when edge 0 feeds node 1.
